_documentation.what_is_this: Project-scoped MCP servers. Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor auto-load this file from the project root. User-scoped MCPs (configured in Claude.ai, Codex settings, etc.) load globally and don't need to be listed here.
_documentation.do_you_need_this_file: Often NO. If you (and your collaborators) already have the MCPs you want connected at the user/web level, leave `mcpServers` empty. This file then serves as documentation: which MCPs are worth considering for this archetype, and how to wire them up if a friend or fresh environment needs them. Add a server here only when you want it scoped to THIS project (e.g. a project-specific Linear/Notion workspace, or a fresh setup that lacks your globals).
_documentation.how_to_use: Move servers from `_examples` into `mcpServers` to activate them. Don't commit secrets — prefer OAuth-based MCPs (browser-handshake, no inline tokens) where available. For MCPs that require a token, use env-var substitution or keep `.mcp.json` gitignored.
_documentation.review_cadence: Re-check this file when aligning a new project, when the tech stack changes, or every few months — new MCPs ship constantly.

_examples._comment: Copy any of these into `mcpServers` to activate. Each block is self-contained.

context7._when_to_use: Any project using a non-trivial framework or library. Returns up-to-date docs and avoids stale-training-data answers.

astro-docs._when_to_use: Astro projects. Official Astro docs MCP.

svelte._when_to_use: Svelte / SvelteKit projects. Official Svelte MCP.

next-devtools._when_to_use: Next.js projects. Provides Next-specific tooling and docs.

chrome-devtools._when_to_use: When live UX, layout, or perf inspection is needed against a running site.

playwright._when_to_use: Site / app automation, end-to-end interaction, screenshot capture.

cloudflare-worker-mcp-example._when_to_use: Pattern reference: a custom remote MCP on a Cloudflare Worker, authenticating via browser-based OAuth (no inline tokens). Replace the URL with your own worker. mcp-remote runs locally as a stdio bridge and handles the OAuth handshake automatically — first run opens a browser, subsequent runs use the cached token.
